receipt.input: Supplied revision 13 candidate texts, pinned public package and coordinator rulings, including the registry lookup successor fix. All records, identities and credentials are synthetic.
receipt.execution: This revision was authored without tools, test execution, workspace access, network use or target inspection. No target material was encountered. Authored expectations are not observed results.
receipt.receiver: Apply the five ordered replacement arrays and independently run contract/run.py in all four modes. The ruling_checks map identifies default-run assertions. Challenge the registry lookup independently with an observer that enumerates the correct rows but still resolves a retired tuple after migration or restart. The expected result for that observer is exit 1 naming X-REGISTRY-SEEDS and the offending step and lookup. Review downstream obligations with the scope owner.
receipt.limits: The bundled observer is a replaceable synthetic positive control. An independent control pass would establish fixture and oracle agreement. Installed HA and producer parity require reviewer-side evidence. The two reservoir profiles and both seeded registry stores are synthetic.
receipt.forecast_field_report: The work order reports two Unknown observations. No corresponding upstream payload or HA trace was supplied.

wire_basis.legacy: swagger-v1.yaml securitySchemes names api-secret hash header, token URL parameter and temporary bearer. Individual legacy modes here are configured fixture capabilities. The document's top-level combined security stanza alone does not prove each site's anonymous or individual credential policy. properties.js requires entries and treatment read permissions for the selected properties route.
wire_basis.v3: auth.md uses the subject token in the v2 authorization request path and a JWT in the Authorization header for protected v3 reads until expiry. swagger-v3.yaml documents the public version route, the protected collection routes, 401 for JWT authentication failure and 403 for a subject lacking permission. An explicitly configured mixed mode uses its own legacy credential only on legacy routes. A 403 remains observable without silently serving legacy data. Destination and method are asserted from the actual request log against cases.json.

g180.basis: Both Entry schemas and the bgnow delta ruling. Latest valid 180 mg/dL at noon minus the preceding 162 is +18. Duplicate, non-SGV and out-of-order inputs leave the measurement and source direction unchanged.

delta-17.basis: Revision 13 and bgnow.js. The noon mean of 180 minus the 11:55 mean of 163 is +17 mg/dL.

delta-negative.basis: bgnow.js scales the means independently. The current 9.0 minus previous 10.0 is -1.0 mmol/L. The wire display string is -1.

delta-absent.basis: Revision 13 and bgnow.js bucket scan. Noon glucose is available. Either no older reading or an isolated 11:40 sample leaves the delta attribute absent.

delta-interpolated.basis: Revision 13 and bgnow.js. The 20 mg/dL change over ten minutes yields the five-minute prior estimate of 170 and delta +10.

delta-zero.basis: Identical qualifying means at noon and 11:55 produce a present numeric zero delta.

g184.basis: Both Entry schemas distinguish the measured value, measurement timestamp and direction. This recovery payload supplies a newer SGV with all three changed.

gmmol.basis: Revision 13 and Nightscout units.js and bgnow.js. Independently scaled means are 10.0 and 9.0 for either 162 or 163 mg/dL history. The displayed numeric delta is +1.0 mmol/L, with +1 as the native wire display string.

g401.basis: swagger-v3.yaml 401 and the work order's visible protected authorization failure.

g403.basis: swagger-v3.yaml 403 for a subject lacking permission. The fixture uses a restricted credential and the protected resource remains unavailable.

site-mg.basis: swagger-v1.yaml Status.Settings and Threshold. This observation presents server thresholds in their source scale, consistent with ar2.js scaling inputs from mg/dL before display.

site-mmol.basis: swagger-v1.yaml Status.Settings and Threshold. The site declares mmol display independently of which calculations are present. Raw thresholds remain separately labeled in their source scale.

derived.basis: properties.js, iob.js, cob.js and basalprofile.js as cited in revision 13. Calculated IOB and COB have individual offered clocks. Effective basal is 1.2 U/h with no offered measurement time. Scheduled basal is 0.8 U/h and the uploaded values are separate.

derived-partial.basis: properties.js projects the current snapshot. A successful warm poll keeps new IOB and clears omitted COB and basal with their old times.

derived-empty-cob.basis: An empty offered COB object has no calculated amount. Treatment-derived IOB can lack mills. Effective zero is valid despite a nonzero scheduled basal.

derived-unavailable.basis: Revision 13 distinguishes failed calculation reads from successful partial properties. The status route is independent.

derived-zero-cob.basis: A successful calculation after a failed read restores current offered values. Numeric zero COB without a source clock stays numeric with a null timestamp.

f15.basis: ar2.js publishes predicted points with mills and mgdl. The work order anchors the horizon on the current reading. An exact synthetic point at 12:00 plus 15 minutes is 207 mg/dL.

f30.basis: ar2.js publishes predicted points with mills and mgdl. The exact synthetic point at 12:00 plus 30 minutes is 231 mg/dL, also when polled ten minutes after that reading.

f-shift-15.basis: ar2.js centerline is encoded at nominal +2000 ms. Revision 13 publishes 12:22 for the +15 point of the 12:07 SGV. An exact nominal encoding agrees when it carries the same value.

f-shift-30.basis: The 12:37:02 native point yields 231 at nominal 12:37 from the 12:07 measurement, independent of the 12:11 poll and the other horizon.

fu15.basis: Revision 13 requires independent Unknown for a missing anchor, an absent or off-grid +15 point, or conflicting qualifying +15 values. Uploaded loop forecasts are a separate source.

fu30.basis: Work order requires an independent Unknown at +30 when there is no corresponding AR2 point or no usable reading time. An uploaded loop forecast is a separate source.

t-original.basis: Both Treatment schemas describe timestamp, carbs and insulin. v1 exposes _id and v3 fallback exposes the same value as identifier. The bounded read uses gte and lt explicitly. Select the latest valid nonfuture numeric amounts, coalesce repeated source IDs and expose the bounded calendar chronologically.

t-edited.basis: swagger-v3.yaml DocumentBase.identifier is stable across updates. The work order requires the comparable legacy reread to show the edited record with the same identity. Its time and the independent carbohydrate record stay fixed.

t-deleted.basis: The v1 and v3 treatment APIs support deletion. The work order requires removal across successive polls. These are complete bounded snapshots, and the next valid insulin treatment is lower at 11:00.

t-future-latest.basis: Revision 13 preserves historical latest values at the noon clock even when the source contains future treatments with larger or newer amounts.

t-future-event.basis: Nightscout Treatment duration and HA CalendarEntity overlap contract. One 20-minute event runs from 12:30 to 12:50. Duplicates coalesce, and the 12:45 window preserves original times.

t-future-boundary.basis: HA timed overlap has two strict inequalities. Starting exactly at window end or ending exactly at window start gives an available empty result.

t-calendar-unavailable.basis: Revision 13 requires complete calendar pagination. A successful first page followed by a failed page leaves calendar unavailable while historical latest values are independently available.

i84.basis: insulinage.js picks the latest nonfuture insulin change and uses whole elapsed hours. Jan 5 00:00 to Jan 8 12:00 is 3 days and 12 hours.

i6.basis: insulinage.js and the work order. Jan 8 06:00 to 12:00 is 6 h. Equal-time matching duplicates have the same observable timestamp and age.

i-unknown.basis: insulinage.js has found=false when no eligible change exists. The work order maps a missing event to Unknown on a successful read.

i-unavailable.basis: The work order distinguishes a failed treatment read from a successful search with no matching marker.

c84.basis: cannulaage.js and the v3 Treatment Site Change example. Jan 5 00:00 to Jan 8 12:00 is 84 h.

c6.basis: cannulaage.js uses the newest matching nonfuture site change. The fixture's latest is at 06:00, six hours before the clock.

s84.basis: sensorage.js accepts a valid Sensor Start alone. Jan 5 00:00 to Jan 8 12:00 is 84 h.

ss6.basis: sensorage.js picks a valid Sensor Start when it is later than the Sensor Change. Here 06:00 precedes the poll clock by 6 h.

sc6.basis: sensorage.js marks Sensor Start found=false when Sensor Change is at or after it, so both the later-Change and equal-time cases show Change at 06:00 and 6 h.

b84.basis: batteryage.js uses battery change treatments. A battery percentage is separate telemetry. Jan 5 00:00 to Jan 8 12:00 is 84 h.

b6.basis: batteryage.js uses the latest nonfuture battery treatment. The 06:00 marker is 6 h old.

other-ages-unknown.basis: cannulaage.js, sensorage.js and batteryage.js distinguish missing markers. The work order makes missing event age Unknown.

ages-seven.basis: The four age plugins count elapsed hours. At 13:00 each surviving 06:00 marker is seven hours old. Sensor Change takes the equal-time tie.

ages-fallback.basis: Revision 13 complete recovery after latest markers are removed recomputes all ages from the surviving January 5 markers. Jan 8 at 13:00 is 85 hours later.

ages-unavailable.basis: An incomplete response or an outage supplies no authoritative complete snapshot. All four affected ages are unavailable with cleared observable times and marker attributes.

r-aaps-before.basis: AndroidAPS 4.0.0 Dana status producer as cited in revision 13. The configured upload source's integer 25 U is stamped at its last pump-data time, 299 seconds before the poll.

r-aaps-boundary.basis: The last pump-data timestamp is exactly 300 seconds old, within the synthetic inclusive cutoff.

r-aaps-clock-control.basis: The same 23 U row is usable when the fixture deliberately selects its distinct serialization clock under the 600-second profile override.

r-aaps-other.basis: An explicit binding to the competing upload source selects that source's last pump-data timestamp and amount from the same response.

r-zero.basis: pump.js explicitly retains zero and swagger-v1.yaml defines pump.reservoir as numeric. In the fixture binding, A at 11:57 is newer by measurement than A at 11:53 even when the older measurement arrives later. B is separate.

r-before.basis: Synthetic reservoir parameters. 11:50:01 is 599 seconds before 12:00 and 37.25 U is retained at measurement time.

r-boundary.basis: Synthetic reservoir parameters. 11:50:00 is exactly 600 seconds before 12:00 and is within the inclusive fixture cutoff.

r-unavailable.basis: Revision 13 synthetic binding rejects ages 601 or 301 seconds at the respective cutoffs, future or missing selected timestamps, missing, nonnumeric or nonfinite amounts, and unbound sources. Upload and serialization times and competing sources do not fill a failed binding.

g-unavailable.basis: The work order requires the affected entity to become unavailable on a failed poll and recover at the next successful poll. Site configuration is fetched separately.

g-unknown.basis: The Entry result can be a successful empty array. The normalized observation distinguishes the absence of a current measurement from a transport or decoding failure.

identity-first.basis: HA Core 2026.6 registry tuple and row identity. Capture four distinct, structurally valid registry rows from actual fresh observations.

identity-same.basis: HA registry restore preserves the same-store lookup tuples, row IDs, user-facing entity IDs and customizations for all four roles without duplicates.

identity-fresh.basis: An independent empty store for the same synthetic site resolves the same integration tuples. Row IDs and public names are local to that store.

identity-seed.basis: A sanctioned fixture-owned registry seed supplies all four baseline rows and user customizations. Registry enumeration must equal the original stored rows.

identity-migration.basis: HA Core unique-ID migration retains registry row identity. The synthetic migration changes the three sensor unique IDs to their v2 keys and preserves the calendar tuple, all public entity IDs and user customizations.

lookup-alpha-before.basis: The HA Core 2026.6 tuple lookup contract resolves the original alpha tuples to their seeded row IDs. The future glucose key has no row before migration. Results follow the alpha-before query order in cases.json.

lookup-alpha-after.basis: The public HA migration test retires the old unique-ID tuple. Each migrated sensor tuple resolves only under its v2 key to the same seeded row ID immediately after migration and after the persisted restart. The unchanged calendar lookup still resolves. Results follow the alpha-after query order in cases.json.

lookup-beta.basis: HA Core lookup and restore behavior preserve the independently seeded beta tuples and row IDs across a same-store reload. Results follow the beta query order in cases.json.

A-EXCHANGE-WIRE.missing_rule: Installed server version and adapter credential routing and renewal parity are unobserved.
A-EXCHANGE-WIRE.public_evidence: Revision 13 cites the pinned v2 exchange handler, JWT NumericDate claims and v3 security handler.
distinguishable_observations: Protected reads recover with a new bearer after rejection.
The installed adapter reuses the rejected bearer or sends credentials to another surface.
A-EXCHANGE-WIRE.smallest_decision: Review a sanitized installed-adapter exchange and protected-request trace, including one unexpected 401.

G-DELTA-ROUNDING.missing_rule: The installed adapter's displayed delta parity is unobserved.
G-DELTA-ROUNDING.public_evidence: Pinned bgnow.js and units.js define per-mean scaling. The HA numeric attribute is a revision 13 ruling.
distinguishable_observations: The installed mmol/L delta is numeric +1.0 and -1.0 in the two directions.
It is rounded after subtracting raw SGVs, or emitted as a display string.
G-DELTA-ROUNDING.smallest_decision: Observe the installed adapter against the signed controls in both unit modes.

G-DELTA-MISSING.missing_rule: The installed adapter's handling of missing history and its deployed delta source are unobserved.
G-DELTA-MISSING.public_evidence: Pinned bgnow.js qualifies older buckets and omits delta when no prior mean qualifies.
distinguishable_observations: Current glucose stays available with delta absent and a genuine zero stays present.
The installed adapter supplies a default zero or retains an old delta.
G-DELTA-MISSING.smallest_decision: Observe no-history, older-history and measured-zero polls and record the actual calculation source.

D-CALCULATED-BINDING.missing_rule: Which offered properties and source clocks the effective installed producer provides remains unobserved.
D-CALCULATED-BINDING.public_evidence: Revision 13 cites v2 projection and the IOB, COB and effective basal producer paths.
distinguishable_observations: The adapter follows effective basal and distinct offered calculation clocks.
It follows scheduled basal, controller uploads or a fabricated clock.
D-CALCULATED-BINDING.smallest_decision: Observe a sanctioned populated response and HA output where schedule, effective rate and upload differ.

D-PARTIAL-WARM.missing_rule: Installed warm refresh and transport-failure parity are unobserved.
D-PARTIAL-WARM.public_evidence: The pinned sandbox rebuilds offered properties and v2 returns its current projection.
distinguishable_observations: A successful partial refresh clears missing values while status stays available.
The adapter retains older calculations or makes site status unavailable.
D-PARTIAL-WARM.smallest_decision: Observe populated, partial, failed and recovered polls on one installed adapter session.

F-AR2-NATIVE-OFFSET.missing_rule: The origin of the two field Unknown observations remains unverified.
F-AR2-NATIVE-OFFSET.public_evidence: Pinned ar2.js documents the native +2000 ms centerline. The work order supplies no associated payload or adapter trace.
distinguishable_observations: An installed adapter receives native points with a dated SGV and publishes both nominal horizons.
The wire lacks qualifying input or qualifying points exist and the adapter yields Unknown.
F-AR2-NATIVE-OFFSET.smallest_decision: Capture the dated SGV, projected AR2 property and both adapter observations in one sanitized poll.

F-AR2-TOLERANCE.missing_rule: Installed horizon qualification for off-grid and conflicting inputs is unobserved.
F-AR2-TOLERANCE.public_evidence: Pinned ar2.js defines the native schedule. Revision 13 freezes the two accepted timestamp encodings and conflict rule for this contract.
distinguishable_observations: Only an unambiguous qualifying horizon resolves.
An off-grid point, conflict or uploaded loop point supplies a value.
F-AR2-TOLERANCE.smallest_decision: Replay the boundary and conflict probes through the installed adapter.

T-CALENDAR-FUTURE.missing_rule: Installed adapter coverage and pagination parity are unobserved. Other event inclusion and end semantics for nonpositive or absent durations remain outside this ruling.
T-CALENDAR-FUTURE.public_evidence: Nightscout date filters apply to event starts. HA CalendarEntity specifies strict overlap for timed events.
distinguishable_observations: A prior-start duration-bearing event overlaps and preserves original times.
The adapter misses the event or exposes a partial result after a later page fails.
T-CALENDAR-FUTURE.smallest_decision: Observe a sanctioned overlapping window and a failed later page against the installed adapter. Escalate any broader duration or event-type rule to the scope owner separately.

M-PRUNE-WARM.missing_rule: Installed adapter treatment snapshot completeness and warm retention are unobserved.
M-PRUNE-WARM.public_evidence: Nightscout documents autopruning and stateless age projections from eligible marker lists.
distinguishable_observations: A complete empty snapshot clears the age and a failed read marks it unavailable.
The installed adapter retains a pruned marker or interprets an incomplete read as deletion.
M-PRUNE-WARM.smallest_decision: Observe complete, incomplete and recovery snapshots around a warm prune and restart on the installed adapter.

R-TANDEM-BINDING.missing_rule: Production reservoir feature gate still needs effective producer version, approved source identity, timestamp field, freshness cutoff and boundary policy.
R-TANDEM-BINDING.public_evidence: Nightscout documents reservoir, clock and status time. Its global upload-time filter is distinct from the fixture. Cited AndroidAPS 4.0.0 Dana code uses an uploader label, serialization clock, last pump-data timestamp and integer IU amount.
distinguishable_observations: The sanctioned deployment uses the approved uploader and freshness at its chosen timestamp.
It chooses a competing uploader, upload or serialization time, or a different cutoff.
R-TANDEM-BINDING.smallest_decision: Approve an effective producer version or sanitized specimen and the production binding, time and freshness policy, then observe adapter parity. An uploader label does not establish physical pump identity.

X-HA-REGISTRY-BASELINE.missing_rule: Released target lookup keys, customizations and migration or alias policy require an untouched installed baseline.
X-HA-REGISTRY-BASELINE.public_evidence: HA Core 2026.6 documents tuple lookup, stable registry row IDs, aliases and unique-ID migration that removes the old lookup key. The seeds here are synthetic.
distinguishable_observations: Upgrade preserves the original row, entity ID and user customizations on the same installed store, and live tuple lookups follow the approved migration policy after restart.
Upgrade allocates a replacement row or a tuple designated for retirement still resolves even though the registry enumeration is correct.
X-HA-REGISTRY-BASELINE.smallest_decision: H2 must capture a sanctioned sealed pre-upgrade specimen from a real untouched HA run and approve which installed tuples migrate, remain or retire. Apply the same relational enumeration and lookup oracle to the candidate on that store through restart.
